focus: Repo-root resolution across four cwd scenarios: findRepoRoot vs resolveProjectRoot vs getDefaultWorkspaceRoot

label: The continuity save path validates a --project-root it is given but never validates the default it computes: CONFIG.PROJECT_ROOT comes from resolveProjectRoot, which returns the shared runtime checkout when the caller's project is not a git repository, and resolveProjectRootOption would have refused exactly that path as outside the working repository. Reproduced: resolveProjectRoot('/tmp/rr-probe/bare/nested') returned /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled, which is not inside the cwd, so the same value supplied via --project-root throws.

usesSpecKit tests a bare directory (existsSync of .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit) and only under .skilled, while the shared repo-root module states the sentinel must be a real authored file because a directory sentinel is self-perpetuating, and accepts both .skilled and .opencode. Reproduced: a sibling git repo carrying only .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md gives findRepoRoot = that repo but resolveProjectRoot = the runtime repository plus a stderr note. This also closes the iteration-8/13 residual: usesSpecKit requires that directory and nothing about specs/.

findRepoRoot's DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH of 14 plus its final '?? resolve(start)' makes an unreachable sentinel indistinguishable from a proven root. Reproduced: with the sentinel 12 levels above the start the repo root is returned; at 15 levels the leaf directory itself is returned with findSourceRoot null. No test catches it because the suite's maxDepth assertions are satisfied by the fallback chain rather than the capped walk (maxDepth 0 executes zero loop iterations).

One directory has two absolute spellings across the two resolvers: resolveProjectRoot returns git's realpath'd --show-toplevel while findRepoRoot returns path.resolve of a walked path. Reproduced on a sibling that symlinks .skilled: /private/tmp/rr-probe/sib-linked vs /tmp/rr-probe/sib-linked. Equality, cache-key and startsWith prefix checks between the two misfire on any ancestor symlink, /tmp on macOS being the everyday one.

gitTopLevel swallows every failure in a bare catch, so a non-existent cwd, a missing git binary and a genuine not-a-repo all become null, after which resolveProjectRoot writes a stderr note asserting the project 'is not inside a repository that uses spec-kit' and returns the runtime repository. Reproduced with a non-existent cwd. A typo in a cwd therefore redirects writes to the shared checkout and reads as an opinion rather than an error.

check-goal.cjs carries a fourth root algorithm: getDefaultWorkspaceRoot is path.resolve(__dirname,'../../../../../') with no walk, sentinel, git check or fallback note, and exactly one consumer feeding packet labelling and resolveGoalBudget. Evaluating that expression at a one-level-shallower install depth returns '/', so the budget root silently becomes the filesystem root. Nothing breaks if it is removed in favour of findRepoRoot(__dirname): identical at the shipped depth and sentinel-correct elsewhere.

findRepoRoot's three-way tail (nearestSentinelHolder, hoistAboveOpencodeTree, resolve(start)) collapses to a plain string, so none of the 24 import sites can distinguish a proven root from the depth-cap guess or the non-git echo. Proposed extension: export findRepoRootDetailed returning {root, via, depth} and keep findRepoRoot as a thin wrapper, which changes no caller and is the enabler for the depth-cap and non-git findings rather than a parallel fix.

Scenario (a) nested in this repo and (b) inside .opencode: findRepoRoot = repo root, findSourceRoot = .skilled, resolveProjectRoot = repo root. All three agree; .opencode/skills is a symlink to ../.skilled/skills so the .opencode start reaches the same tree.
Scenario (c) sibling copying .skilled: both resolvers return the sibling and findSourceRoot returns its .skilled. The intended vendored case works.
hoistAboveOpencodeTree returned the repository root for an in-tree path and null for a folder with no source-root segment; nothing this iteration contradicts its documented contract.

runtime/hooks/lib/workspace/repo-root.mjs is a 14-line re-export of six names from ../../../../shared/workspace/repo-root.mjs, not a duplicate implementation: distinct md5, no symlink. The 24 import sites split into a shared-path family and a hooks-shim family and both resolve to the same module today.

direction: Duplicate root-resolution algorithm between the shared module and the hooks copy
reason: runtime/hooks/lib/workspace/repo-root.mjs is an 811-byte re-export shim with a different md5 from the 7048-byte shared module; ls -la and readlink show no symlink, and its export list is exactly the six shared names. Divergence is not duplication here.

direction: hoistAboveOpencodeTree as the cause of the wrong-root results
reason: It returned the repository root for an in-tree path and null outside a source tree on both inputs tried; the wrong roots in this iteration come from findRepoRoot's depth-cap tail and from usesSpecKit, not from the hoist.
